General Notes: Series of weight changes in place, one per beat, with strong pressure into the ball of foot, heel just off or lightly touching the floor; toe not raised. Normally 4 steps (Man RLRL, Lady LRLR) but more or fewer may be used for phrasing or as a link between figures. No turn or gradual turn up to 1/4 to L or R over 4 steps; partner on outside of turn takes very small chassés. PP or CPP shape and high, medium or low elevation may be used (BF footwork if lowered). May end in PP with last step to side (Man 1/8 to L, Lady 1/8 to R) to precede Promenade Close, Huit or Grand Circle. Silver: timing 12&34 adds an extra step to change feet. Precedes/follows any figure ended/commenced with feet together.

Series of very small steps forward or back (no longer than the dancer's foot), one per beat, danced like Sur Place with strong pressure into the ball of foot. Danced in place of Sur Place to travel slightly, achieve alignment or fit phrasing; normally 4 to 8 steps. Chart shows Man forward (Lady back); the backward version is Man RF back, LF back, RF back, LF back (Lady fwd). No turn or gradual curve up to 1/4 (up to 1/2 over 8) to L or R. PP shape with lowered joined hands when turning L, CPP shape when turning R. May end in PP (last step to side, Man 1/8 to L) to precede Promenade Close, Huit, Grand Circle or Spanish Line.

A Paso chassé is two steps (side, close); more or fewer may be danced for phrasing. Danced with strong pressure into the ball of foot. No turn or gradual curve to L or R (up to 1/4 to L). Elevations: Chasses danced with change of height (high on toes with straight legs, or feet flat with knees flexed), e.g. 2 chassés up and 2 down, 1 up and 1 down, or 1 step up and 1 down; PP shape may change to CPP shape with each change of height. Precede: Sur Place, Promenade, Sixteen, Chasse Cape. Follow: Sur Place, Attack, Fallaway Reverse Turn, Coup de Pique, Chasse Cape; if curved to face against LOD, Separation.

Commenced with an Appel, then LF side, RF close, LF side (Lady opposite). Steps 3-4 may be repeated. Follow by closing RF to LF into a LF Sur Place (or Appel closing RF to LF on 1), then any figure commenced with feet together. If last step is taken to side in PP (Man 1/8 to L, Lady 1/8 to R): Promenade Close, Huit, Grand Circle, Spanish Line. No turn or gradual curve to L or R (up to 1/4 to R). Elevations as for Chasses to Right.

General Notes: ISTD lists Deplacement (also Attack). Man steps fwd on 1 (Lady back), then turns 1/4 to L to side and close. Elevation may be used on 4, rising high on toes. May also commence facing DC or DW; 1/8 to L may be used between 2-3 to achieve alignment. Alternative: 3 fwd walks RLR (Lady back LRL) and close with no turn. Silver-Gold styling: by count 2 lower joined hands in an outward circular movement to hip, returning to normal hold over 3-4. Useful to achieve alignment for the following figure.

The Attack is the Deplacement commenced with an Appel on 1. Slip Attack: step 1 danced as a Slip Appel turning up to 1/2 to L. Knees flex at end of step 1 and remain lowered through the figure (older Laird charts); Man may lower L arm in a circular movement to waist level on 2-4. Elevation may be used on 4. Precede: Sur Place, Promenade, Sixteen, or any figure ended with feet together. Follow: Sur Place returning to normal height, or any figure commenced with feet together. Steps 2-4 of Attack plus a RF Sur Place form Ending 1 of the Syncopated Separation.

May also commence facing LOD or DW. Steps 3-4 commenced in PP form the Promenade Close.

Figure Name: Overturned Change of Places Left to Right
General Notes: Development of Change of Places L to R. On 5 Man lowers L arm and turns Lady strongly L by rotating hand to R from wrist (palm outwards); Lady continues an extra 1/2 to L on RF in a spiral, LF crossing loosely in front, ending in Tandem Position in front of Man. On 6-8 Lady dances a forward lock or 3 small runs; at end of 8 Man turns Lady to R (1/4 to R on LF) to face him. Follow with Chicken Walks, Simple Spin or figures commenced in Open Position; Lady normally dances a Flick (or Point) Ball Change in place of 1-2 of Link.
